The original generate.py, manifest.json, synthetic inputs, and every generated
.fit and .zip file in this directory are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0
Universal: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

To the extent possible under law, the authors waive all copyright and related
rights in this original synthetic corpus. It is supplied without warranty.

No recorded activity, personal FIT file, GPS position, private device identity,
secret, environment file, official Garmin SDK, or production data is included.
All timestamps, device identifiers, developer identifiers, measurements, and
application identifiers are invented test values. Manufacturers and sport enum
values identify format semantics, not actual devices or users.

The generator uses Python's standard library only. Field numbers, scales, enum
values, protocol framing, and CRC arithmetic were inspected in publicly
available protocol references and fitparser 0.11.0's MIT-licensed profile.
No fitparser source code or packaged activity fixture is copied into this corpus.
Source references and independent arithmetic oracles appear in manifest.json.

progressive_rr_input.json is an immutable copy of the Runs analysis author's
original synthetic progression. The author explicitly authorizes CC0 dedication.
Its software generator uses NumPy 2.2.6 PCG64 seed 7429 and an AR process:
rho = 0.97 - 1.57*t/480; state = rho*state + standard_normal();
intervalMs = 600 - 270*t/480 + 3*state; t advances by intervalMs/1000.
The committed JSON provides the complete input without needing NumPy.
The FIT generator quantizes cumulative beat times to 1/1024 second and encodes
native packed HR events with a timestamp, fractional, and full counter anchor.
RR intervals come from event counter differences, never reciprocal heart rate.

progressive_rr_oracle.json is the same author's independently computed,
CC0-authorized software-only numerical reference. Its comparator uses SciPy
1.15.3 smoothness-priors lambda 500 and MIT-licensed nolds 0.6.3 OLS DFA.
No comparator implementation is copied, and neither dependency is needed
to regenerate FIT. The reference distinguishes raw intervals from packed
1/1024-second quantized intervals; numerical tolerances are not physiological
precision claims.

The original garmin_progressive_rr.fit deliberately demonstrates no-extrapolation:
its fitted 0.50 crossing falls beyond the candidate's observed HR range, so LT2
is absent even though an algebraic line intersection exists. Manifest numerical
references distinguish fitted intersections from admissible threshold results.

progressive_rr_positive_input.json and progressive_rr_positive_oracle.json are
distinct CC0-authorized inputs from the same author, using6ms rather than3ms
AR-process amplitude with the same seed and linear ramp. They generate the
separate progressive_rr_positive.fit. Its independent encoded-input numerical
reference has one admissible candidate for each threshold without changing the
no-extrapolation rule or weakening numerical tolerances.

Reproduce from repository root:
python3 apps/api/tests/fixtures/runs/generate.py

The manifest records generator version, fixed corpus seed, features, licenses,
provenance, field dictionary, byte counts, and SHA-256 hashes. Regeneration
uses no clock, randomness, network, installed FIT parser, or external file.
